_meta.indication: VILTEPSO is indicated for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) in patients who have a confirmed mutation of the DMD gene that is amenable to exon 53 skipping, approved under accelerated approval based on an increase in dystrophin production in skeletal muscle.

pivotal_trials.phase: Multicenter, 2-period dose-finding study (conducted in the United States and Canada)
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, 2-period dose-finding study. The initial 4 weeks were a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled period in 8 patients (3:1 randomization; 6 on viltolarsen and 2 on placebo), in two sequentially-enrolled dose cohorts of 40 mg/kg/week (n=8) or 80 mg/kg/week (n=8). After Week 24, all patients continued in an open-label extension study (Study NS-065-202) at their previously randomized dose of either 40 mg/kg/wk or 80 mg/kg/wk.
pivotal_trials.population: Male patients aged 4 to <10 years with an established clinical diagnosis of DMD and a genetic mutation amenable to exon 53 skipping, on a stable dose of corticosteroids, able to walk independently.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from Baseline to Week 25 in dystrophin protein levels in biceps muscle biopsy samples, determined by western blot analysis.
pivotal_trials.n: 16 patients participated in the study. In the initial 4-week randomized, placebo-controlled period, patients were randomized 3:1 (6 on viltolarsen and 2 on placebo) within each of two dose cohorts (40 mg/kg/wk, n=8; 80 mg/kg/wk, n=8); all patients then received open-label viltolarsen.
pivotal_trials.result: A statistically significant increase in dystrophin from baseline was observed after 20 to 24 weeks of treatment at both 40 mg/kg and 80 mg/kg by western blot. In patients receiving VILTEPSO 80 mg/kg once weekly, mean dystrophin increased from 0.6% of normal at baseline to 5.9% of normal by Week 25, a mean change of 5.3% (median change 3.8%; p=0.01) by validated western blot.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥15%) were upper respiratory tract infection (63%), injection site reaction (25%), cough (19%), and pyrexia (19%). The main labeled warning is kidney toxicity based on animal data.
target_moa: Viltolarsen is an antisense oligonucleotide with a phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer (PMO) backbone designed to bind exon 53 of dystrophin pre-mRNA to alter splicing, restore the mRNA reading frame, and induce production of de novo truncated dystrophin protein.

advisory_committee.vote: This application was not referred to an advisory committee because the safety profile was acceptable, the trial designs were acceptable, and the findings on the surrogate marker were clear.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Increase in dystrophin production in skeletal muscle (dystrophin biomarker), proposed as a surrogate endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.

summary.text: Viltepso received accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.500 based on an increase in dystrophin production in skeletal muscle as a surrogate endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit, with a required confirmatory Phase 3 trial (NS-065/NCNP-01-301) to verify clinical benefit. The NME application had Priority review and an orphan drug designation for the DMD indication.
